prs.title: Handle Sonos coordinator moves, session takeovers and announcement clip status
prs.author: mnestrud
prs.ci: green on 05cc0aeb5
prs.merge_state: Based on dev 99b616327; merge-tree clean against origin/dev 3ebf1e10b. GitHub: MERGEABLE, BLOCKED on review.
prs.tldr: _leads_moved_group is now re-checked synchronously after the wait, connection included, so a role given up again is left alone. The flow-load timeout decline holds, because aiosonos create_session can hand back the same session id. Our PROBLEM still stands: a play preparing audio on either player has not bumped cloud_queue_item_generation yet, so the hand-over transfers over it. Checking ATTR_PLAY_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS on both queues fixes it without touching core. Copilot resolved all three threads and has no open issues. Sonos is excluded from auto-approve.
prs.summary: r4333309129: commit 07c354954 moves the readiness predicate into _leads_moved_group (connected, client.player.is_coordinator, group subscribed). _hand_over_moved_group calls it again after _wait_for_moved_group, with no await between that check, the generation/_plays_queue checks and the start of the hand-over. Parametrised tests cover role, status and connection loss, so the fix is verified. r4333309191 (declined): aiosonos 0.1.15 _play_stream_url runs create_session and then load_stream_url, and create_session can return the previously used session id. After a CommandTimeout, the provider cannot tell a timed-out create (old session still active) from a timed-out load into a reused session. Forgetting the queue is the conservative choice. The play command already raised, so the user sees the failure. Decline OK. r4333309171 (declined): holding core playback locks from a provider risks lock-order inversion with transfer_queue's own cmd_ungroup/stop calls, so fixing it in core transfer_queue is the right home. The justification is only half-true, though: core's _transfer_ad_hoc_leadership runs inside cmd_set_members under the old leader's PLAYBACK lock (players/controller.py:1404), and only the new leader is unguarded there. Our PROBLEM is the concrete harm from that gap. Scenario: the user starts a play on either speaker right after the move, and handle_play_action holds the lock and sets ATTR_PLAY_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS while audio prepares. play_media has not run yet, so neither generation has moved. The hand-over then forgets our queue, transfer_queue clears and moves it, and play_index cancels the user's pending play or moves their new items to the other speaker. The suggested patch bails when either queue has the flag set. It is a synchronous check right before the transfer and has been validated: 195 sonos tests pass, and the new test fails without the fix.
blockers: Our PROBLEM f1 still stands: the hand-over can override a user play still preparing audio. `fix 6779` pushes the validated patch (skip the hand-over while either queue shows a play in progress), or post it
GPT Sol's new point (f2): stream resolution changes queue ownership before the URL is resolved

findings.title: Hand-over overrides a play still preparing audio
findings.detail: cloud_queue_item_generation only moves inside play_media, which runs after the core play action has prepared audio under the queue lock. A user play started on the old or new coordinator in the hand-over window passes every check, then transfer_queue clears/moves the queue and play_index cancels the user's pending play_index or plays the user's new items on the other speaker. Core's own leader hand-over holds the old leader's PLAYBACK lock, so the Sonos path is less guarded than core.
findings.fix: Before forgetting the queue, return when queue.extra_attributes[ATTR_PLAY_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS] is set on either queue_id or new_coordinator.player_id (patch below). The full lock fix stays a core follow-up in transfer_queue.

findings.title: Stream resolution can leave ownership on media never sent to Sonos
findings.detail: _play_stream clears the previous queue and session binding and assigns the incoming _flow_queue_id before awaiting resolve_stream_url, outside the load-settlement try. If resolution fails or is cancelled, Sonos keeps playing the previous queue while MA remembers the replacement with no session. Claude did not flag this.
findings.fix: Resolve the URL before changing queue ownership.

findings.title: Reused session on a flow-load timeout is read as a failed load
findings.detail: GPT Sol rated this a PROBLEM; Claude thinks the decline holds since aiosonos can't tell which step timed out and forgetting the queue is the safe default.
findings.fix: Keep uncertain ownership until reconciled, or have aiosonos expose the load result.

prs.title: Retry provider loads after a connection failure without a traceback
prs.author: balloob
prs.ci: test fails on ca070d415: the new test_connection_failure_is_retried_without_traceback (1 failed, 16976 passed). lint passed.
prs.merge_state: BLOCKED (draft), mergeable, no conflicts with dev
prs.tldr: When a provider can not reach its service at load time (network not up at boot), the loader logged a full traceback and never retried. This PR treats aiohttp.ClientConnectionError as retryable with the normal backoff and logs it as one line unless verbose logging is on. The code change is 5 lines and correct. The new test is broken, so CI is red. The PR body still has a traceback dump, Claude footers and an unticked checklist that the bot flagged.
prs.summary: mass.py change is sound. ClientConnectorError passes through _provider_load_step unchanged because it has a message, so the new isinstance check sees it. It changes the retry contract that until now only retried MusicAssistantError, which is the right call for transient network errors. The test fails for a test-only reason: it uses the mass fixture with _demo_music_provider, but that manifest is not loaded in tests, so get_provider_config raises KeyError and load_provider returns before it ever loads. I confirmed that locally. tests/core/test_provider_load_retry.py already has a _mass_with_load_error helper for exactly this; moving the test there makes it pass (patch below). Copilot's TLS point (ClientSSLError and fingerprint mismatch now retried) is weak: the retry backs off to 120s, and a cert failure at boot is often a wrong clock that fixes itself. Its wrapped-cause point is real but partial: a SetupFailedError raised from an aiohttp error still logs a traceback. That can be a follow-up. The PR description needs the cleanup the bot and Copilot asked for.

prs.tldr: Draft that swaps the squeezelite sync corrector for an LMS port living in aioslimproto#558 and routes CLI transport commands through the player controller. Blocked on the unmerged aioslimproto PR (currently a git pin to the author's fork), and it drops the WiiM pause workarounds without a replacement.
prs.summary: The provider now delegates group start (SyncGroup.start, unpause_at on a shared player-clock instant) and drift correction (SyncGroup.check, play points plus reference player) to a new aioslimproto module, maps CONF_SYNC_ADJUST to the client's play_delay, and removes the old average-elapsed corrector. The sign convention of the sync delay is preserved (positive still makes the player play earlier). The linked issue (drift after start/pause/seek from the jiffies clock mapping) is addressed at the right layer, since the new epoch tracking fixes the clock mapping rather than patching symptoms. A second change routes legacy CLI transport commands through mass.players so a control on a synced member acts on the whole group, which is a sensible use of the existing cli_command_handler seam. The provider code is small and clean. The real work and risk sit in aioslimproto#558, which is open with no reviews and whose author asks for design discussion on whether sync belongs in the library. The PR also drops both WiiM workarounds (explicit pause before group start, pause()+unpause_at instead of pause_for), and #558 says itself that it does not replace them.

findings.title: WiiM/LinkPlay sync group members regress: early start and stuck after pause_for
findings.detail: The removed code carried two WiiM workarounds. It paused players after play_url for group playback because WiiM starts early despite autostart=0, and it used pause()+unpause_at() instead of pause_for because WiiM does not auto-resume from strm p. Both are gone. SyncGroup.check in aioslimproto#558 calls client.pause_for() for any player that is ahead, and the #558 description says the WiiM case is deliberately left for later. A WiiM member that drifts ahead gets paused and stays silent. On start it can also begin before the coordinated unpause_at.
findings.fix: Fix it in aioslimproto#558 before merging: have SyncGroup.check correct 'ahead' players with pause() followed by unpause_at(jiffies + delta), which works on all devices and matches what the old provider helper did. Or add a per-client pause_for fallback the provider can enable. Keep the explicit pause() after play_url for group members until start behaviour on WiiM has been checked with the new SyncGroup.start.

prs.tldr: Fixes Roku Media Assistant queue stalls (stale queued slot, false track-change detection, one-shot enqueue) and reports IDLE when the stream freezes at its end. Code looks right and was tested by the author and kees, but it is a draft, Verify fails on unticked checkboxes, and it ships no tests although kees wrote them.
prs.summary: All changes are in the Roku player. play_media and stop now clear the local queued item and reset elapsed tracking, matching the app which drops its queued deeplink on every new deeplink. poll only swaps current media to the queued item when something is queued and the position falls back by more than 10 s, which removes the old abs() check that fired on every fresh play and blanked the current track when nothing was queued. enqueue_next_media retries up to three times, which makes sense since the stream feeder hands the next item over once and marks it enqueued regardless. The end-of-stream detector (PLAYING, position at duration minus 1.5 s, unchanged for 10 s) gives MA the PLAYING to IDLE transition it needs for end-of-queue handling, autoplay and dynamic refill. Note that MA does not advance mid-queue on IDLE, so for a track whose enqueue failed the player now shows IDLE instead of a stuck PLAYING, it does not skip ahead. That is still an improvement. kees verified the behaviour on a current dev nightly and wrote five unit tests that fail on dev and pass with this change. The approach is sound and scoped to the provider. What is left is housekeeping.

prs.tldr: Big provider-icon audit (92 files) that adds dark/monochrome variants and a documented icon convention, but a meaningful chunk of the new 'monochrome' icons don't follow the convention they introduce (opaque backgrounds or grayscale gradients instead of a flat white silhouette on transparent), and the linked issue's named examples (chromecast, sonos) are still unaddressed pending maintainer input.
prs.summary: The PR audits provider icons project-wide: it adds missing icon_dark.svg/icon_monochrome.svg files, replaces a few outdated logos (amplipi, msx_bridge, etc.), lightens airplay, drops six baseline entries for icons now under the 5 KB budget, and documents the icon.svg/icon_dark.svg/icon_monochrome.svg convention in DEVELOPMENT.md and the three demo providers. The size-budget work checks out: every touched svg is at or under the 5 KB cap in the worktree, and the six entries removed from scripts/lint_baselines/oversized_provider_icons.txt correspond exactly to files that were shrunk (verified against the pre-PR baseline). The approach for most of the 92 files is right and CI (including the pre-commit icon-size check) is green. The problem is that around a sixth of the new/rewritten icon_monochrome.svg files don't actually match the 'white silhouette on a transparent background' rule this same PR writes into DEVELOPMENT.md: some (ai_radio, ariacast_receiver, nts, openai_compatible, smart_playlist) keep an opaque black/white background rectangle covering the whole canvas, and some (itunes_artwork, itunes_podcasts, jellyfin, nugs, filesystem_onedrive, bbc_sounds, musicbrainz, yandex_smarthome, yandex_station) are grayscale versions of the original colored/gradient artwork rather than a flat white shape. Both patterns will look wrong on the frontend's dark-as-is/light-inverted rendering (a floating box, or a washed-out gray badge, instead of a clean silhouette) and at least a couple (itunes_podcasts, ai_radio) are demonstrably just the colored icon.svg with its fill colors swapped to black/white, background box included. Separately, the linked issue (backlog#158) specifically calls out chromecast and sonos as icons that need dark-surface treatment; the PR doesn't touch either, and the author says so directly in the description, proposing a follow-up PR with a different approach (frontend fallback to monochrome) instead. That's a reasonable plan but it's still an open question for the maintainer, not a decision already made.

findings.title: New monochrome icon is the colored icon.svg with colors swapped, background box included
findings.detail: This file is byte-identical in structure to icon.svg with `fill="#18bcf2"` -> `fill="#fff"`, `stroke="#ffffff"` -> `stroke="#000"`, and the two accent fills -> `#000`. The opaque `<rect x="-5" y="-5" width="34" height="34" fill="#fff">` background is kept as-is. Per the DEVELOPMENT.md text this PR adds, icon_monochrome.svg should be a white shape on a transparent background that the frontend shows as-is on dark surfaces and inverts on light ones; with an opaque background this renders as a solid box sitting on the surface instead of a silhouette, and inverting it doesn't fix that. Same opaque-background pattern in ariacast_receiver/icon_monochrome.svg (new file, white rounded-rect bg + black glyph), nts/icon_monochrome.svg (new file, black rect bg + white glyph), openai_compatible/icon_monochrome.svg and smart_playlist/icon_monochrome.svg (both new, white rect bg + black glyph).
findings.fix: Drop the background rect/shape and draw the glyph itself in a single flat white fill, matching the existing convention (e.g. spotify, tidal, tunein, deezer icon_monochrome.svg all ship a bare white path with no background).

findings.title: Monochrome icon is a grayscale recolor of the branded gradient, not a white silhouette
findings.detail: The diff shows the only change to this file's gradient stops was `#F452FF`/`#832BC1` (the podcast app's purple/magenta) recolored to `#bababa`/`#9b9b9b`, keeping the linear gradient. A gray gradient isn't invertible the way a flat white fill is, and it won't read as a clean silhouette on either surface. Same issue in itunes_artwork/icon_monochrome.svg (new file, gray radial/linear gradients), jellyfin/icon_monochrome.svg (gray linear-gradient fill), nugs/icon_monochrome.svg (gray linear gradients), filesystem_onedrive/icon_monochrome.svg (seven gray radial gradients), bbc_sounds/icon_monochrome.svg (multiple flat gray fills like #b7b7b7, #a8a8a8), musicbrainz/icon_monochrome.svg (flat grays like #afafaf, #9e9e9e), yandex_smarthome/icon_monochrome.svg (#a3a3a3 fill) and yandex_station/icon_monochrome.svg (gray linear gradient).
findings.fix: Replace the gradient/gray fills with a single flat white fill (`fill="#fff"` or `fill="#ffffff"`) on a transparent background, redrawing the shape as a silhouette where the gradient currently carries the design.

findings.title: Linked issue's named examples (chromecast, sonos) are left unaddressed

prs.author: afeldman1
prs.ci: lint and test fail on the 09-19 run. mypy: missing CONF_* names in audiobookshelf/storytel/gpodder, method-assign in jellyfin; ruff I001 x4; tests/providers/audiobookshelf fails to import.

prs.tldr: Adds a Quick Connect sign-in option to the Jellyfin setup flow, next to username and password. After OzGav asked for the shared MA constants in Jellyfin, the author also removed local CONF_USERNAME/PASSWORD/VERIFY_SSL from audiobookshelf, gpodder and storytel. That cleanup breaks those providers' imports and is why CI is red. OzGav asked on 09-30 why other providers are touched and got no answer. Copilot's stale-token CRITICAL is still open and the branch conflicts with dev.
prs.summary: The Quick Connect flow itself is reasonable: initiate, poll /QuickConnect/Connect inside external_until with a 10 minute deadline, then trade the secret for a token and store token, user id and device id in setup_data. There are real problems though. (1) The cross-provider constants cleanup is out of scope and broken: audiobookshelf/__init__.py and storytel/__init__.py still import CONF_PASSWORD etc. from their own constants modules, gpodder/setup_flow.py imports names gpodder/__init__ no longer exports, and the audiobookshelf tests fail to collect. That answers OzGav's question: it overshoots his 09-16 request, which was only about Jellyfin. (2) Copilot's CRITICAL is valid. The reconfigure finish handler (controllers/config/flows.py:546) merges new values into the stored setup_data, so the pop() calls do nothing. Switching from Quick Connect back to password keeps the old access_token, and handle_async_init prefers it. (3) JellyfinConnection/_use_current_url_authentication monkeypatches a private aiojellyfin method (mypy method-assign) to send ApiKey. That repeats what #6251's _normalize_jellyfin_media_url already does on the PR's own base, and it has nothing to do with Quick Connect. (4) Quick Connect uses mass.server_id as the raw device id. The manifest is multi_instance, and Jellyfin revokes older tokens on the same device id, so two Quick Connect instances against one server would log each other out. (5) The copy_text plumbing in models/setup_flow.py duplicates #6268. (6) On dev, #6382 changed setup errors to pass the SetupFlowError object, so the rebase needs the new errors pattern. I verified the suggested patch locally: jellyfin init tests plus the audiobookshelf/gpodder tests pass (20 passed), and mypy is clean on the four providers. The jellyfin parser snapshot failures also happen on the merge base, so they are a venv model skew and not this PR.

prs.title: Stop a Sendspin player reporting a position ahead of what it is playing
prs.author: caraar12345
prs.ci: All green on the head (lint, test 2m17s), but that run predates dev's #6271 and the branch now conflicts.
prs.merge_state: DIRTY (conflict: sendspin/player.py)
prs.tldr: Recomputes the Sendspin flow timeline anchor on every commit, so the reported position and the beat schedule follow aiosendspin's forward rebase after a producer stall. It also prunes late-join history against the push-stream clock. The core one-line anchor fix is sound. The beat-schedule refresh machinery around it still has four open Copilot CRITICALs on the head. OzGav moved it back to draft on 09-23 for those, and the author has been silent since. It also conflicts with dev's #6271 metadata-generation guard in _send_beat_schedule.
prs.summary: The central change is _timeline_start_us = commit_start_us - produced_audio_us on every commit. It holds steady when nothing stalls and absorbs a rebase on the next commit, which is correct and minimal. flow_track_anchor_us benefits automatically. The pruning change is also right: chunk start_time_us is already on the push-stream clock, so cutting at now - _HISTORY_KEEP_PAST_US keeps committed-but-unplayed audio for late joiners. The old formula effectively cut relative to the commit tail. The weak part is the beat-schedule re-publish (on_flow_timeline_rebased, _pending_anchor_delta_us, _anchor_rebase_pending). It runs in a separate task id from the metadata refresh, so a same-track refresh that captured the pre-rebase anchor can finish after the rebase refresh, overwrite it and clear the pending state. The live_media check only catches track changes. The 500 ms per-commit threshold also never fires for repeated smaller same-direction shifts. Copilot's sub-second update_state point is acknowledged in the code comment and is acceptable. The retry-exit case (analysis unavailable for an item that already had beats) is real but unlikely, because analysis is cached. Dev's #6271 added a takeover generation guard in exactly the conflicting spot. The rebase should keep both checks and could reuse a refresh generation to fix the ordering. Stable has the same stale-anchor bug. The PR description is a long AI narrative, and Copilot asked for it to be trimmed.
blockers: Merge conflict with dev #6271 in sendspin/player.py _send_beat_schedule (keep the _metadata_publish_allowed(generation) guard).
Copilot CRITICAL: concurrent same-track beat refreshes can publish a pre-rebase anchor (player.py:2254, valid, open).
Copilot CRITICAL: sub-threshold rebases never accumulate toward the 500 ms beat refresh (playback.py:923, valid, open).
OzGav drafted on 09-23 for outstanding Copilot comments. No author activity since.

findings.title: Beat refreshes are not ordered within a track
findings.detail: The rebase refresh (task sendspin_beat_rebase_*) and the metadata/retry refresh use different task ids. Both await get_audio_analysis. The post-await check only compares queue_item_id, so an older same-track refresh, or one from before a seek, can publish last and clear _pending_anchor_delta_us.
findings.fix: Bump a beat-refresh generation on every rebase, seek or media update. Capture it before the await and drop the result if it changed. Or route all refreshes through one task id with abort_existing=True.

findings.title: Per-commit threshold misses cumulative small rebases
findings.detail: anchor_rebased compares each commit's delta with 500 ms. Two 400 ms rebases move the timeline 800 ms but never trigger on_flow_timeline_rebased, so the beat schedule stays off. Elapsed time is fine because the anchor itself updates.
findings.fix: Track the drift since the last reported anchor and fire when that total crosses the threshold, then reset it.

findings.title: Retry loop exits early after a rebase refresh with no analysis
findings.detail: When analysis returns None the schedule is cleared, but _last_beat_queue_item_id still names the item, so _beat_retry_loop returns immediately as if beats were pushed. Analysis is cached for an item that already had beats, so this is unlikely in practice.
findings.fix: Reset _last_beat_queue_item_id when clearing the schedule in that branch.

findings.title: Very long explanatory comments
findings.detail: Several 10-line comments narrate the debugging. The repo prefers short why-comments.
findings.fix: Cut each to one or two lines and move the background to the PR description.

prs.title: Cast dashboard support for the MilkDrop visualizer
prs.author: jozefKruszynski
prs.ci: All green on head 018900c6b (lint, test, CodeQL, audit, provider-scope). Locally the dashboard, airplay, milkdrop, chromecast and fully_kiosk suites pass (1190), plus the update_user_profile auth tests.

prs.tldr: Lets the MilkDrop visualizer run on cast dashboards, following the casting user's visualizer_* preferences behind a per-show secret viewer_key. Both last-round Copilot CRITICALs are fixed properly: the key rotates on every show and AirPlay now gets one too. Copilot's new CRITICAL on a mid-launch race does not hold, because viewers re-fetch on the sessions-updated event fired right after commit, so it needs a decline reply. One previously-missed item is real: a repeated self preference change on the same websocket emits no event, so cast viewers get stuck. That is a three-line fix.
prs.summary: The rotation fix is correct. The key is popped before on_show so the consumer's own resolve mints a new one, and on failure the failed key is dropped and the previous one put back, which matches the display still showing the old cast. The API path (no on_show) also gets a fresh key via get_url. The AirPlay change is safe: the tvOS app's LaunchIntent keeps route only to derive player, so extra dashboard_id and viewer_key params are ignored, and the server log still prints only the target origin. Copilot r4234225739 says the new key is valid while _sessions and _session_owners still describe the previous cast. True in the code, but only the display being launched holds the new url, it was already showing that caster, and _signal_sessions_updated right after commit makes the frontend re-fetch viewer_preferences (frontend#2617 subscribes to DASHBOARD_SESSIONS_UPDATED). So the worst case is a sub-second flash of the old caster's preset on the same screen. Decline. Previously missed, auth.py:1608: verified. For a self-update target_user is the websocket's _authenticated_user, cached at connect and never refreshed, so preset A to B then back to A on one connection diffs A against A and skips the event. Viewers stay on B until something else fires. Fix: diff against the stored row. Validated with a regression test that fails before and passes after. Previously missed, migration capped at 1000 users by list_users: not realistic for a home server, skip. Previously missed, log sanitizing only CR and LF: NEL and U+2028 are a cosmetic log-viewer nit, optional. The previous card's previously-missed items (migration location, _resolve_display sanitize, description trim) no longer appear in Copilot's list. The older SUGGESTION on backgrounded receiver relaunch still stands as optional.

suggested_fix.description: Diff preferences against the stored user so repeated self-updates on one websocket still notify viewers, with a regression test (fails before, passes after). Then decline r4234225739: "The new key is only reachable from the url the display itself is launching, and that display was already showing the previous caster. show_dashboard signals sessions-updated right after it commits the new session and owner, and the viewer re-fetches viewer_preferences on that event, so a viewer that fetches mid-launch is corrected within the same show. +            previous_preferences = (stored_user or target_user).preferences
             target_user = await self.update_user_preferences(target_user, preferences)
             # cast dashboards render with their casting user's preferences; notify viewers
             self.mass.dashboard.notify_user_preferences_changed(

prs.summary:
I ran 7708abc0b (old queries) and 94553624f (new queries) against the same seeded dataset in throwaway worktrees and compared the output. The dataset had 4000 play_history rows: library, instance, domain and unmapped providers, a domain id shared by two library tracks, alias artist credits, fractional timestamps, plays around DST changes and a second user. The comparison covered top_items for 7 media types, genre/decade distribution, listening_time by artist and genre, plays_over_time hour/day/week/month, listening_activity and 519 play_count probes, across today/week/month/year/all_time and UTC, Amsterdam, New York, Kathmandu (+5:45) and Lord Howe (30-minute DST). All 1030 cases matched exactly. The week start `((bucket + 3) / 7 * 7 - 3)` and weekday `(bucket / 24 + 3) % 7` give Monday-start weeks and 0=Monday for epoch-day buckets. The 900 s non-UTC bucketing matched per-play conversion in every zone I tested. Dropping DISTINCT from the album and genre CTEs is safe because album_tracks, genre_media_item_mapping and provider_mappings all have unique constraints. EXPLAIN shows the time-series and played_pairs scans run as a covering-index SEARCH. No cache_statistics, use_cache, invalidate_statistics_cache, generation dict or merge/playlog hook is left. 'statistics' is still missing from CORE_CONTROLLER_ATTRS, so get_diagnostics is dead code. _get_period_cutoff already sits on _StatisticsBase in statistics/base.py, so not moving it further is fine.

prs.title: Local files: import the rating embedded in file tags
prs.author: kiwipaulrob
prs.ci: green
prs.merge_state: BLOCKED (review required), merges cleanly with origin/dev
prs.whats_new: Still a draft, head a061a4657 unchanged. kiwipaulrob replied to OzGav at 17:23Z: popularity is int | None and providers fill it with very different scales (radiobrowser click counts, 0-100 elsewhere), so a half-step 0-10 rating doesn't fit. The PR only sets the favorite flag. Long term they want a separate, editable rating field in the database, and say they'll fork if that's not wanted. That's a design call for you or Marcel.
prs.tldr: Adds an opt-in setting to the local files provider that turns a rating stored in file tags (ID3 POPM, Vorbis RATING, MP4 rate) into the existing like/dislike favorite flag, with two thresholds. The direction is fine and matches the Plex approach OzGav agreed to in discussion 6678. In its current form it does nothing for anyone who already has a library: it only runs for files that are new to the index, and the toggle is off by default. The three settings have no strings, so the UI shows raw keys. Vorbis ratings on the common 1-5 scale import 5 stars as a dislike.
prs.summary: New core helper music_assistant/helpers/rating.py (POPM byte or 0-100 value to a 0-10 rating, then rating to tri-state favorite). helpers/tags.py reads POPM (max over frames), Vorbis RATING and MP4 rate or freeform RATING. filesystem_local adds 3 config entries (enable, favorite >= 8.0, dislike <= 2.0) and sets track.favorite only when prev_checksum is None. base.add_item_to_library already records the favorite only for new library items, through favorites.record_from_provider, which never overrides a user's own choice. So the prev_checksum guard adds nothing, and the PR never reaches files that were already indexed. Not provider-scoped: it adds a core helper and touches helpers/tags.py, so it is not auto-approve eligible. No models or API schema change. 136 tests pass locally (new rating tests plus test_tags.py). CI is green.
blockers: No backfill: rating import only applies to files new to the index, so existing libraries (the main use case) get nothing when the option is turned on
The 3 new config entries have no strings.json entries, so the UI shows raw keys
Vorbis RATING is always read as 0-100, so foobar2000-style 1-5 ratings import 5 stars as a dislike
Nearest-anchor POPM mapping is non-monotonic (100 -> 5 stars, 102 -> 3 stars, 60 -> 3 stars, 64 -> 2 stars)
6 open Copilot findings on the head, none answered yet

findings.title: Existing libraries never get their ratings imported
findings.detail: The option is off by default and is not in the setup flow, so every library is indexed before a user can turn it on. Later syncs skip unchanged files, and add_item_to_library records a favorite only for a new library item. Turning the option on therefore has no effect on files already in the library. The prev_checksum guard is also unnecessary, because record_from_provider already never overrides a user's own choice.
findings.fix: Drop the prev_checksum guard. When the option is enabled, or the thresholds change, run a one-time pass over the indexed tracks: re-read the tags and call mass.music.favorites.record_from_provider for each rated file. This needs a decision from maintainers on where the backfill lives.

findings.title: Missing strings for the 3 new config entries
findings.detail: rating_import_enabled, rating_favorite_threshold and rating_dislike_threshold have no config_entries keys in filesystem_local/strings.json, so the options UI has no label or description.
findings.fix: Add the three keys to filesystem_local/strings.json and regenerate translations/en.json with scripts.build_translations (patch attached).

findings.title: Vorbis RATING read only as a percentage
findings.detail: foobar2000 and several other taggers write Vorbis RATING as 1-5. With the 0-100 assumption, RATING=5 becomes 0.5 and is stored as a dislike under the default threshold of 2.0. That is the opposite of what the user set.
findings.fix: Read values 1-5 as a star count (value * 2) and values above 5 as 0-100. Add a parser-level test that builds real Vorbis tags.

findings.title: POPM nearest-anchor mapping is non-monotonic
findings.detail: Mixing three tagger ladders breaks POPM's higher-is-better rule: 100 maps to 5 stars while 102 maps to 3, and 60 maps above 64. The iTunes ladder this works around is not something iTunes writes into POPM. WMP, MusicBee, MediaMonkey 4+ and Picard all use the WMP values, which the standard bands read correctly.
findings.fix: Use the standard WMP read bands (1-31, 32-95, 96-159, 160-223, 224-255). That keeps the mapping monotonic and drops the 22-entry anchor table.

findings.title: MP4 rate atom only works when it is stored as UTF-8 text
findings.detail: mutagen 1.48.1 has no parser for 'rate'. Unknown atoms are kept only when they are UTF-8 text and are dropped otherwise. The branch works for text-typed atoms, but there is no test that uses a real M4A.
findings.fix: Add a parser test with real MP4Tags, or limit support to the freeform RATING tag.

findings.title: Duplicates the Plex helper
findings.detail: favorite_from_rating has the same logic as plex/helpers.get_favorite_from_rating. Fine for this PR. Plex can move to the shared helper in a follow-up.
findings.fix: Follow-up: make Plex use helpers.rating.favorite_from_rating.

findings.title: Long module docstring and PR body
findings.detail: The module docstring describes future plans (the inverse direction). The PR body is very long. Copilot flagged the same thing.
findings.fix: Trim the docstring to what the module does now.

prs.tldr: Some AirPlay 1 receivers stay silent when a Sendspin live input restarts, even though the RAOP transport is fine. A PROGRESS command restores audio, but live inputs often have no metadata, so the existing metadata path never sends one. The PR schedules a PROGRESS anchor 100 ms after every acknowledged RAOP start, with a generation counter so stop, flush or a newer start drop stale anchors. The code is small and the tests pass (212 in test_stream.py). Blockers are the unticked template checklist that fails Verify and two open Copilot threads.
prs.summary: Adds _send_start_progress_anchor to AirPlayStream. On a RAOP route, start() spawns a task that sleeps until the acked audible instant plus 100 ms, takes the metadata lock, checks the generation and connection, and sends PROGRESS=<start_position + elapsed>. stop() and flush() bump the generation. AirPlay 2 starts are unchanged. On normal tracks this does not double up with the post-start media-updated progress, because _last_progress_sent is set and the later push is deduped by the 2 s threshold. Hardware evidence is from the author's local hotfix on a Sonos One SL and an older Klipsch receiver; the generalized patch itself has not been run on them yet.

prs.summary: Delta e2882279a..306c090ad, one commit, controller.py and the pin test file. (1) _apply_native_volume_pin now catches non-MusicAssistantError from player.volume_set and raises PlayerCommandFailed, same pattern as handle_player_command in players/helpers.py. Register and register_or_update keep their MusicAssistantError catch, so device errors no longer abort registration. This resolves our previous blocker and Copilot r4280705863 without touching providers. (2) The CONF_VOLUME_CONTROL and CONF_NATIVE_VOLUME reads moved inside the per-player VOLUME lock, which resolves r4280705925. save_player_config writes storage before calling on_player_config_change, so the recheck sees the new values. get_player_lock is per-task reentrant, so no self-deadlock, and the pin only takes the member lock, so no group/member inversion. The new asyncio test does catch the old ordering: after sleep(0) the old code had already read the pin before blocking. (3) New issue from (2): the early return now happens inside the lock, so every VOLUME_SET player takes its VOLUME lock on each register/register_or_update. Both calls run under the global _register_lock. If a volume command is stuck on that player (likely on a reconnect after a drop), registration of every player waits up to PLAYER_LOCK_TIMEOUT (30s), even though the pin is not configured. GPT Sol flagged the same thing as PROBLEM. Fix: cheap pre-check before the lock, recheck inside (patch below). (4) Pin before set_config: author kept it and replied on the resolved thread r4254688831. Fine. prs.author: trudenboy
prs.ci: All green on 0d643083b (lint, pytest 1-3, provider-scope, audit).

prs.tldr: Out of draft again since 08:52Z and OzGav is re-requested. All 58 review threads are resolved, and the three OzGav points from September (owner_player_id rename, conftest.py removed, deferred import removed) are done in the code. Scope is clean: only the new provider, its tests and en.json keys. Two real bugs remain against the current AudioSource session model. The plugin never calls deselect_source, so a second cast on the same renderer reuses the first cast's cached stream details (with the codec ffmpeg detected), and a DLNA Stop leaves the player showing the DLNA source. Also, any stream teardown during Pause is treated as Stop.
prs.summary: New plugin provider synced from ma-provider-dlna-receiver v1.2.8. It runs one aiohttp UPnP server per MA player (ports from 8298 upward, on one detected IPv4) and one SSDP advertiser per renderer, each with its own UDP 1900 socket (SO_REUSEPORT). Playback goes through play_media with an AUDIO_SOURCE uri, and get_audio_stream proxies the sender's URL. Files touched: only music_assistant/providers/dlna_receiver/*, tests/providers/dlna_receiver/* and 9 new keys in translations/en.json. No core changes. Conventions are mostly fine: get_config_entries is an instance method on dev's model, the registry uses the event bus, tasks go through mass.create_task, and narrow excepts are used. The VERSION file matches other synced providers (yandex_*, kion_music, msx_bridge). The docs URL in the manifest returns 404 until music-assistant.io#626 merges. Unload cancels the metadata task, unsubscribes the player events, sends byebye, closes both UDP transports, stops the aiohttp runner, cancels GENA tasks and leaves mass.http_session open. GPT Sol and I found no leak. Security of the unauthenticated endpoint is reasonable for DLNA: SetAVTransportURI and GENA callbacks are validated against loopback, link-local, multicast and reserved addresses on every redirect hop, redirects are capped at 5, GENA is capped at 32 subs per service with a 1800 s TIMEOUT clamp, and SOAP/DIDL parsing rejects DOCTYPE/ENTITY and anything over 64 KiB. Anyone on the LAN can still play to and set the volume of every exposed player. That is inherent to DLNA and the plugin is opt-in. The remaining issues are about the newer AudioSource session contract. Sessions survive cmd_stop and keep session.streamdetails on re-select (_start_audio_source_session with preserve_details). ffmpeg writes the detected codec into that AudioFormat in place, so the next cast on the same renderer is launched with the old -acodec. Other receivers (airplay_receiver, spotify_connect, ariacast, sendspin_source) call deselect_source with the session's playback_session_id when their session ends. This plugin does not. on_source_unselected also sets STOPPED and clears elapsed on every stream teardown, but dev documents that a paused source's stream can be torn down while the source stays selected.

No deselect_source on Stop or on a new cast: the stale streamdetails/codec reuse bug.
Pause plus stream teardown is reported as STOPPED and the position is lost.

findings.title: Second cast on the same renderer reuses the first cast's stream details
findings.detail: play_media of the same AudioSource keeps the existing AudioSourceSession (audio_sources.py _start_audio_source_session, preserve_details=True), and the stream handler only calls get_stream_details when session.streamdetails is None. ffmpeg's apply_stream_info and audio.py:4470 write the detected codec into that AudioFormat in place. Casting FLAC and then MP3 to the same renderer launches the MP3 stream with -acodec flac. The fresh UNKNOWN format from get_stream_details is never used. Same for the placeholder stream_metadata. GPT Sol found this; I traced it on dev.
findings.fix: Before play_media in the fresh-start branch, release this provider's session on the player with mass.players.deselect_source(..., stop_playback=False, provider_instance_id, source_id, playback_session_id), the way airplay_receiver does.

findings.title: DLNA Stop leaves the DLNA source selected on the player
findings.detail: _on_stop only calls cmd_stop. Source sessions survive a stop. Only _release_audio_source/deselect_source end them. After the sender stops, the player keeps reporting the DLNA source and old metadata, and its own queue stays inactive. Other receivers call deselect_source when their session ends.
findings.fix: Use deselect_source(stop_playback=True) with the session's playback_session_id, then clear_playback. See suggested_fix.

findings.title: Stream teardown during Pause is treated as Stop
findings.detail: on_source_unselected fires in the stream handler's finally block, so it runs whenever the HTTP stream closes. Dev's contract says a paused source can have its stream torn down while it stays selected. Here it sets STOPPED (and NOTIFYs the sender) and clears elapsed, so the next Play takes the fresh-start path and restarts. _on_pause/_on_play also call output.pause()/output.play() directly instead of mass.players.cmd_pause/cmd_play. That skips the player lock, the queue's resume_pos and has_lost_paused_stream handling.
findings.fix: Keep PAUSED state across stream teardown when the renderer is paused (only reset on Stop/new URI or on_source_released), and route pause/resume through mass.players.cmd_pause/cmd_play.

findings.title: DNS rebinding window between validation and connect
findings.detail: validate_outbound_url resolves with getaddrinfo, but mass.http_session resolves again on its own, so a hostile LAN DNS answer can still reach loopback. The code comments already say so. Impact is low: an attacker on the LAN can already drive the unauthenticated renderer, and the GET response only reaches ffmpeg. GPT Sol rated it CRITICAL. I don't think it blocks.
findings.fix: Optional: a connector with a resolver that applies _is_allowed_destination to the addresses it connects to.

findings.title: Renderer volume starts at 50 and never syncs with the player
findings.detail: GetVolume and the GENA RenderingControl state report self.volume, which starts at 50 and changes only through SetVolume. Control points show the wrong volume, and the first slider move jumps the real player.
findings.fix: Read the player's volume_level in GetVolume/initial vars, or subscribe to player updates.

findings.title: Leftover standalone-repo wording
findings.detail: The urls.py module docstring says it exists so tests can run 'without requiring the full MA runtime'. That is the same standalone-repo scaffolding reasoning OzGav asked to drop. eventing.py also keeps an owned-session fallback 'for standalone/test use'.
findings.fix: Trim the docstrings. Drop the owned-session path if only tests use it.

suggested_fix.description: Release the plugin's AudioSource session with deselect_source on DLNA Stop (stop_playback=True) and before a new cast (stop_playback=False), so the session's cached streamdetails and metadata are not reused. Falls back to cmd_stop when the player is not on our source. Existing tests that mock cmd_stop in _on_stop will need an update (Marvin's OK required). The Pause teardown issue is not covered by this patch.
suggested_fix.patch:

index 3773348..b804704 100644

+++ b/music_assistant/providers/dlna_receiver/provider.py
@@ -604,6 +604,8 @@ class DLNAReceiverProvider(PluginProvider):
         # QueueOption.PLAY overrides any user-configured default enqueue
         # option — the sender expects immediate playback, not enqueueing.
         source_uri = create_uri(MediaType.AUDIO_SOURCE, self.instance_id, source_id)
+        # A new cast must not reuse the previous cast's stream details (detected codec).
+        await self._release_source_session(inst, stop_playback=False)
         try:
             await self.mass.player_queues.play_media(target, source_uri, option=QueueOption.PLAY)
         except MusicAssistantError as err:
@@ -634,10 +636,26 @@ class DLNAReceiverProvider(PluginProvider):
 
     async def _on_stop(self, inst: RendererInstance) -> None:
         """Handle Stop for this instance's player."""
-        if inst.player_id:
-            await self.mass.players.cmd_stop(inst.player_id)
+        await self._release_source_session(inst, stop_playback=True)
         clear_playback(inst)
 
+    async def _release_source_session(self, inst: RendererInstance, stop_playback: bool) -> None:
+        """Give up this renderer's AudioSource session on its player, if it still owns it."""
+        if not inst.player_id:
+            return
+        session = self.mass.players.get_audio_source_session(inst.player_id)
+        if session is None or session.provider_instance_id != self.instance_id:
+            if stop_playback:
+                await self.mass.players.cmd_stop(inst.player_id)
+            return
+        await self.mass.players.deselect_source(
+            inst.player_id,
+            stop_playback=stop_playback,
+            provider_instance_id=self.instance_id,
+            source_id=self._source_id_for(inst),
+            playback_session_id=session.playback_session_id,
+        )
+

findings.title: Repeat One never resets the page's song clock in a flow stream
findings.detail: New in v1.1.0, found by GPT Sol, confirmed in _publish_flow_item. A repeated item keeps its queue_item_id and the flow keeps its playback generation, so the guard `shown == (generation, media.queue_item_id)` suppresses the media message for every new pass. The page keeps the first pass's start, so the clock and progress stay capped at the duration (web.js now clamps to current.duration) and synced lyrics stay at the end. Same for Repeat All with a one-item queue. Before v1.1.0 each repeat was a new play_media with a fresh play message. UI only, audio is fine.
findings.fix: Detect a new pass, not only an item change: for example also publish when the queue's elapsed time for the same item drops below the last published value, or key the guard on the queue's flow stream log entry instead of the item id. Add a Repeat One case to test_flow_stream.py.

findings.title: Socket reconnect after HTML5 fallback re-enables Sendspin
findings.detail: Copilot 'previously missed' on 3242e70ec. connectWS always sends sendspin_client_id when one is known. After a successful HTML5 fallback, a socket-only reconnect (Wi-Fi blip, server restart) re-registers the identity, which clears sendspin_fallback and recreates the bridge, while the page runs with SENDSPIN false. The next stream start then opens Sendspin mode again and the connect timeout and fallback repeat, interrupting playback. Plausible from the code, not reproduced. Unchanged in v1.0.35 (web.js not touched); Copilot no longer lists it. Unchanged in v1.0.36. Unchanged in v1.0.38. Unchanged in v1.0.39. Unchanged in v1.0.40. Unchanged in v1.0.44. Unchanged in v1.1.0.
findings.fix: Send the current transport separately from the ownership proof and keep sendspin_fallback across socket-only reconnects; add a reconnect-after-fallback test.

findings.title: Muted kiosk plays Sendspin audio after a reload
findings.detail: New in v1.0.31 (mute support). _send_snapshot returns early in the Sendspin branch without sending mute, and initSendspin creates the SendspinPlayer asynchronously after the welcome message (module load, codec probes), so a mute message that arrives first only mutes the HTML5 element. The new SendspinPlayer starts unmuted and nothing reapplies the mute, while MA still shows the kiosk muted. Same after the Sendspin player is recreated. Found by GPT Sol and us; sendspin-js 5.0.0 does have setMuted. Core routes mute to the kiosk natively (VOLUME_MUTE wins in mute_control), so there is no double dispatch. Unchanged in v1.0.35. Unchanged in v1.0.36. v1.0.38 folds volume and mute into _volume_messages for the HTML5 snapshot, but the Sendspin branch still returns before sending them; web.js not touched. Unchanged in v1.0.39. Unchanged in v1.0.40. Unchanged in v1.0.44. Unchanged in v1.1.0. The new _ws_played shortcut sends volume and mute for HTML5 pages, the Sendspin branch still returns before them.
findings.fix: Send volume and mute in the Sendspin snapshot branch under the outbound lock, and apply audio.muted to a new SendspinPlayer (in the patch).

findings.title: Fallback holds the kiosk playback lock across a universal group resume
findings.detail: New in v1.0.26. When the kiosk is a universal group member, get_group_and_player_lock takes the group lock and the kiosk lock, then resume(queue) restarts the group. UGP play_media starts each member in a TaskManager task that takes the member's playback lock (universal_group/player.py:446). The lock is only re-entrant per task, so the kiosk member waits the 30s non-strict timeout and then runs without the lock. Found by GPT Sol, confirmed in core and UGP code; not run. Unchanged in v1.0.27. GPT Sol checked the new advance lock for the same stall: not reached, UGP sends FLOW_STREAM media without queue_item_id, so the kiosk stops locally. Unchanged in v1.0.28. findings.title: /ws ownership covers the Sendspin key, not the kiosk player
findings.detail: The new X25519 challenge is sound for what it proves: fresh server key and nonce per socket, both ids in the MAC, compare_digest, invalid keys rejected. But a LAN client that knows a kiosk's device_id can still connect without sendspin_client_id; _verify_sendspin_claim returns None and the socket joins that player, gets its stream token and playback generation, and can send seek and ended. The pin also lives only on the live player object: 5s after the last socket closes the player is unregistered and the pin is gone, so the same device_id can be re-registered with another key and inherit the saved player config. findings.title: Seek to the track end: fixed for the page, server seeks rely on core flow handling (Copilot r4302797493, resolved)
findings.detail: v1.1.0 caps seekToSong at floor(dur) - end_margin, with end_margin sent in the welcome message from END_MARGIN. Verified. The kiosk now has no ENQUEUE and plays core's /flow/ stream, so a server-side seek to the exact end (MA frontend, HA, players/cmd/seek) goes queue.seek -> play_index -> a flow that starts with an empty remainder and runs on into the next item. The old failure (empty /single/ stream, playback_reached_end rejected, kiosk IDLE on the finished item) is gone because that code is removed. Left: an exact-end seek on the last queue item gives an empty flow, the page reports ended or an error and the kiosk goes IDLE, which is the end of the queue anyway and matches other flow-mode players (GPT Sol raised this as PROBLEM; we rate it core behaviour, not a kiosk bug). The author mentions a page test for the clamp; it lives in the upstream repo, not in this diff.
findings.fix: None needed in the provider. Optionally clamp position == duration in core queue seek, as a separate core PR.

findings.title: Browser playback failure no longer tears down the queue session
findings.detail: New in v1.0.30. _stop_failed_playback now calls player.stop() locally instead of cmd_stop. That reports IDLE but skips PlayerQueuesController._handle_stop (controller.py:1986-2030), which cancels the preload and enqueue tasks and the prewarm, and releases the session's audio buffers. After a decode or network failure mid-queue the session stays open and an upstream producer can keep a capped provider stream slot until the buffer's idle cleanup (about 300s). Found by GPT Sol, confirmed on origin/dev. The local stop is right for announcements, which is why the lock was dropped. Unchanged in v1.0.32 (provider.py:688 still awaits player.stop()); GPT Sol re-confirmed. v1.0.33 adds a second caller of the same pattern: a current-generation end report short of the song end also calls player.stop() directly. Unchanged in v1.0.35. Unchanged in v1.0.36. Unchanged in v1.0.38. Unchanged in v1.0.39. Unchanged in v1.0.40. Unchanged in v1.0.44. v1.1.0 drops ENQUEUE, so core no longer runs preload or enqueue tasks for the kiosk, and the flow generator ends when the page drops the connection. The local stop still skips _handle_stop, but what is left to clean up is much smaller. Downgraded to SUGGESTION.
findings.fix: Optional: for queue media, spawn a generation-guarded cmd_stop after the local stop so core runs its normal stop path.

findings.title: Page close during a stream refresh skips the other pages
findings.detail: v1.0.38 runs the output move and refresh_stream as provider work (run_owned with asyncio.shield), so a closing page no longer cancels them. That fixes the original point. What is left: the fan-out of the rebuilt stream to the other pages of the player still runs in the cancelled _send_snapshot. If the reconnecting page closes during the refresh seek while another page stays, the refresh swaps the session and generation under suppress_ws_notify, and the surviving page never gets the new play message. Its old stream then ends with a stale generation. Needs two pages on one kiosk and a close inside the seek window. Found by GPT Sol (rated CRITICAL); we rate SUGGESTION. Unchanged in v1.0.39. Unchanged in v1.0.40. Unchanged in v1.0.44. Still present in v1.1.0: the new _close_socket rebuild skips it because the closing page has no _ws_played entry yet, and the fan-out still runs in the cancelled _send_snapshot. GPT Sol rated it CRITICAL again; needs two pages on one kiosk and a close inside the seek window, so we keep SUGGESTION.
findings.fix: Run refresh plus the post to the other pages as one provider-owned step; only the reconnecting page's own snapshot send should depend on its socket.

findings.title: Closing any page restarts the flow on every other page
findings.detail: New in v1.1.0, by design per the code comment: each page opens its own copy of the flow URL and the queue tracks only the last one, so _close_socket rebuilds the flow (a seek) for all remaining pages whenever a page that received the current play message leaves. Closing a second tab therefore gives an audible restart on the main kiosk. Each page also runs its own flow generator, so two pages mean two provider streams. Multi-page kiosks are uncommon.
findings.fix: Ask the author whether multiple pages per kiosk are a supported setup. If yes, consider serving one shared stream per kiosk.

findings.title: Held clock still runs between polls
findings.detail: New in v1.0.39. Found by GPT Sol, confirmed. After 10 s without browser reports the position holds, but poll() publishes it with a fresh timestamp while PLAYING, so core and the frontend extrapolate it again for up to the 5 s poll interval and then snap back (110, 115, 110). _refreshable_stream reads corrected_elapsed_time, so a reconnect seek can land up to 5 s past the held position. Cosmetic in the UI; small skip on reconnect. Unchanged in v1.0.40. Unchanged in v1.0.44. v1.1.0 reads queue.corrected_elapsed_time in _refreshable_stream; that is derived from the same player position, so the small reconnect skip likely remains. Position reports are now every 2 s instead of 5 s, which shortens the window.
findings.fix: Use self._clock_position(time.time()) in _refreshable_stream instead of corrected_elapsed_time. The UI sawtooth is acceptable or needs a non-running state.

findings.title: Paused own-queue handover shows the kiosk idle
findings.detail: v1.0.29 fixes the follower part (Copilot r4285543627, resolved): a paused follower now parks the leader's item and position on the kiosk queue without playing. The non-follower paused case is unchanged: fallback returns after the teardown and the kiosk has no native current_media, so the snapshot shows idle instead of paused. The queue keeps its item and position, so Play still works. Cosmetic. Unchanged in v1.0.30. Unchanged in v1.0.32. Unchanged in v1.0.33. Unchanged in v1.0.34. Unchanged in v1.0.35. findings.title: Per-player send lock is held across send_str
findings.detail: New in v1.0.34. _send_in_order and _send_snapshot hold the player's outbound lock while awaiting ws.send_str. If one page's transport is paused (half-dead Wi-Fi tab), play, pause and stop for the other pages of that player wait until the heartbeat closes it. aiohttp only awaits drain once its write buffer is past the limit, so it needs much unsent data. GPT Sol rated CRITICAL; we rate SUGGESTION. Also, the disconnect cleanup skips a locked entry and never retries (small leak). Unchanged in v1.0.35. Unchanged in v1.0.36. Unchanged in v1.0.38. findings.fix: Keep ordering per socket: one send queue per socket, filled under the player lock, drained without it.

findings.title: Second browser sharing a device_id is closed with 1008 in a loop
findings.detail: New in v1.0.30. The identity rule in _set_sendspin_owner fixes Copilot r4286147571 (verified: all callers run under _player_lock and only the /ws path can hit a conflict; reattach_player builds a fresh player). But two browsers opened with the same ?device_id= URL now get the second one closed with 1008 on every reconnect while the first is live, instead of joining as a non-owner tab. findings.fix: Ask the author whether shared device_id URLs are supported. If yes, attach the socket without the claim instead of closing it.

findings.title: Claim on an already registered kiosk does not take over a universal wrapper
findings.detail: prepare_player adds the kiosk UUID to a one-output universal_player wrapper so core's _check_replace_universal_player migrates it when the kiosk registers. In the existing-kiosk branch of get_or_register_player the kiosk is already registered, and apply_bridge_claim's register_or_update does not re-run protocol linking for a player that is already PROTOCOL. The wrapper then stays. Needs a new browser identity that was already wrapped while its kiosk player is live, so rare. Found by GPT Sol, confirmed in register_or_update. Unchanged in v1.0.30. findings.title: Origin check rejects /ws behind an HTTPS reverse proxy
findings.detail: _reject_cross_site now compares Origin with request.scheme://request.host. aiohttp does not apply X-Forwarded-Proto/Host, so behind a TLS-terminating proxy the browser sends Origin https://host and the server sees http, and /ws returns 403. web.js already builds wss:// URLs for https pages, so the author seems to expect that setup. Plain http://<ip>:8098 works. GPT Sol rated this CRITICAL; we rate it SUGGESTION since the default deployment is plain HTTP. Same check /builder-auth already had, and matches our earlier suggested fix. Unchanged in v1.0.30. Unchanged in v1.0.32. Unchanged in v1.0.33. Unchanged in v1.0.34. Unchanged in v1.0.35. findings.fix: Ask the author if an HTTPS proxy is a supported setup. If yes, compare Origin's host:port with request.host only, or add an allowed-origin option.

prs.author: lawrence-jeff
prs.ci: lint and test (3.11) green on e9350c219. PR Labels Verify fails with 'No labels defined on the pull request': it requires one of breaking-change, bugfix, refactor, new-feature, maintenance, ci, dependencies, and the PR has no label. Adding bugfix fixes it (the workflow also runs on labeled). 49 passed, 2 xfailed in tests/cli_test.py from a git-archive copy.
prs.merge_state: MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE (label check only). Based on current main, merge-tree clean.
prs.tldr: e9350c2 sends waitingToPlay=1 while BUFFERING or BUFFER_READY, as Marvin asked, and Copilot now recommends approval. GPT Sol found a side effect: a gapless handoff (MA's enqueue path) also sets BUFFERING while the current track still plays, so the clock now freezes for the last seconds of every track. Small patch below. Verify fails only because there is no label: add bugfix.
prs.summary: One new commit, e9350c2 'Send waitingToPlay while the player is buffering' (cli.py: 4 comment lines out, 6 code lines in; the test is parametrized over BUFFERING/BUFFER_READY (flag 1, mode play) and PLAYING/PAUSED/STOPPED (flag absent)). It matches our posted comment and Copilot's medium, which Copilot now lists as resolved. lawrence-jeff replied at 22:35Z that he tried it on a piCorePlayer and a Squeezebox Radio: the flag shows briefly at track start and after a seek. Remaining issue, raised by GPT Sol and confirmed against client.py: _process_stat_stmd promotes the enqueued track via play_url(send_flush=False), which sets state BUFFERING (and STMc sets it again) while the current track keeps playing until STMs. During that window, roughly the output buffer (several seconds), the status now carries waitingToPlay=1, and JiveLite holds its clock, so the display freezes near the end of each track and jumps at the next one. MA's squeezelite provider uses that path in non-flow mode (player.py enqueue=True, send_flush=False). Before this commit the client simply ran its clock there. LMS only sends the flag when nothing is audibly playing. Our own earlier patch had the same gap. Fix: a SlimClient.waiting_to_play property that is True in BUFFERING/BUFFER_READY unless a gapless handoff is in progress (_buffering_media set and no flushed start pending), used by cli.py. I have not seen the freeze on hardware; it follows from the code. Label still missing. After merge: aioslimproto release plus server pin bump (aioslimproto==3.3.0 in music_assistant/providers/squeezelite/manifest.json and requirements_all.txt).
blockers: No label: PR Labels Verify fails. Add bugfix.
waitingToPlay=1 is also sent during a gapless handoff while the current track still plays (MA's enqueue path), which freezes JiveLite's clock near each track end. Patch below.

findings.title: waitingToPlay also sent during a gapless handoff
findings.detail: On STMd the enqueued track is promoted with play_url(send_flush=False), which sets state BUFFERING (STMc sets it again) while the current track is still audible until STMs. The status then sends waitingToPlay=1 and JiveLite stops advancing its clock for the rest of the track. MA's squeezelite provider enqueues this way in non-flow mode. Found by GPT Sol, confirmed in client.py; not seen on hardware.
findings.fix: Add SlimClient.waiting_to_play: True in BUFFERING/BUFFER_READY unless _buffering_media is set without a flushed start pending (_awaiting_stream_start False). Use it in cli.py. Patch below with client and cli tests.

diff --git a/aioslimproto/client.py b/aioslimproto/client.py
index 1e89695..4849b6b 100644
--- a/aioslimproto/client.py
+++ b/aioslimproto/client.py
@@ -236,6 +236,14 @@ class SlimClient:
         """Return current state of player."""
         return self._state
 
+    @property
+    def waiting_to_play(self) -> bool:
+        """Return True while playback is about to start and no audio plays yet."""
+        if self._state not in (PlayerState.BUFFERING, PlayerState.BUFFER_READY):

diff --git a/tests/client_test.py b/tests/client_test.py
index 7f26e92..bd9a8f6 100644
--- a/tests/client_test.py
+++ b/tests/client_test.py
@@ -709,3 +709,47 @@ class TestPositionAcrossPauseAndResume:
         await live_client.pause()

+
+
+class TestWaitingToPlay:
+    """Tests for when the player reports it is waiting for audio to start."""
+
+    @pytest.mark.asyncio
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("state", [PlayerState.BUFFERING, PlayerState.BUFFER_READY])
+    async def test_waiting_while_buffering_without_audio(
+        self, client: SlimClient, state: PlayerState
+    ) -> None:
+        """A start, seek or rebuffer has no audio playing until the stream starts."""
+        client._state = state  # noqa: SLF001
+
+        assert client.waiting_to_play
+
+    @pytest.mark.asyncio
+    async def test_waiting_after_a_flushed_start(self, live_client: SlimClient) -> None:
+        """A flushed start waits for the new stream."""
+        await live_client.play_url(_TRACK_URL)
+
+        assert live_client.waiting_to_play
+
+    @pytest.mark.asyncio
+    async def test_not_waiting_during_a_gapless_handoff(
+        self, live_client: SlimClient
+    ) -> None:
+        """The current track keeps playing while the next one buffers."""
+        live_client._state = PlayerState.PLAYING  # noqa: SLF001
+        await live_client.play_url(_TRACK_URL, send_flush=False)
+
+        assert live_client.state == PlayerState.BUFFERING
+        assert not live_client.waiting_to_play
+
+    @pytest.mark.asyncio
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(

+    )
+    async def test_not_waiting_otherwise(

+    ) -> None:

+        client._state = state  # noqa: SLF001
+
+        assert not client.waiting_to_play

prs.title: Let an application add its own routes to the CLI web server
prs.author: lawrence-jeff
prs.ci: green (lint, test 3.11). PR Labels check has not run yet and the PR has no label; it needs new-feature.
prs.merge_state: CLEAN
prs.tldr: Adds an optional extra_routes {path: handler} dict to SlimServer so an app can serve artwork and icons on the CLI web port. Small, additive, tested. Author asks for a design opinion; the hook is the right shape.
prs.summary:
SqueezePlay/JiveLite clients fetch artwork for cover ids (/music/<id>/cover_WxH_m.png), relative icon paths (html/images/*.png) and remote images (/imageproxy/...) from the web server they do JSON-RPC against, which is the aiohttp app aioslimproto owns on cli_port_json. Today nothing answers those paths. The PR lets the app pass in aiohttp routes at construction, registered with method * after /jsonrpc.js and /cometd. Default behavior unchanged. Tests start a real CLI web server and pass locally (4 passed).

Design opinion for Marvin: approve the approach. The serving logic needs MA library and image proxy access, so it belongs in the provider, and the library cannot add routes after start because aiohttp freezes the router. A constructor dict is the simplest API that works and survives stop/start (the app is rebuilt each start and the dict is replayed). Alternatives are not clearly better: a RouteDef list adds method control nobody needs yet, a setup callback leaks the web.Application, and a public add_route still has to buffer until start. Emitting absolute URLs to MA's own web server would cover menu items the provider builds, but not the paths clients generate themselves from a coverid/icon-id (sized /music/<id>/cover_* variants, imageproxy requests, client-side html/images assets), so the hook is still needed.

Points to raise with the author: the docstring's ordering claim is only accurate for aiohttp 3.9 linear matching; 3.10+ resolves by path-prefix buckets (verified in aiohttp 3.13.5). The provider side should match sized cover paths (cover_225x225_m.png style), not only /music/{id}/cover, and the explicit 404 catch-all is redundant since aiohttp already 404s. Merging needs an aioslimproto release plus a server pin bump (server origin/dev pins 3.3.0), and the server provider does not pass cli_command_handler or extra_routes yet; the author's provider rework is not in a server PR yet.
blockers: No label (needs new-feature for the PR Labels check and release drafter)
Author asked for a design decision; needs Marvin's reply

findings.title: Route ordering docstring is not accurate on aiohttp 3.10+
findings.detail: aiohttp 3.10+ resolves via a resource index keyed by path prefix, walking from the longest prefix down. Registration order only matters within one bucket, and a plain path is not always tried first (e.g. '/' and a root catch-all share the '/' bucket). The advice 'catch-all last' is still correct and portable.
findings.fix: Say routes are registered in dict order, matched by aiohttp's rules, and a catch-all should come last.

findings.title: Collisions with /jsonrpc.js or /cometd behave inconsistently
findings.detail: An extra '/cometd' right after the built-in reuses that resource and add_route raises at start(); an extra '/jsonrpc.js' creates a second, unreachable resource silently. Unlikely in practice since the only consumer is the MA provider, so not a blocker.
findings.fix: Optional: skip or reject the two reserved paths with a clear error in __init__.

findings.title: Failed re-validation leaves an earlier event subscription live
findings.detail: GPT Sol: if an already-authenticated socket sends a second auth with token B and B is revoked during validation, the new loop clears _authenticated_user and unregisters the client, but the subscription from the first auth stays active. The socket keeps receiving events while unauthenticated and untracked, so later revocations can't reach it. Narrow: needs a re-auth on a live socket plus a revocation inside the window. Copilot raised the same at 01:52Z as CRITICAL (r4309722568): player_access_filter(None) removes player restrictions for the leftover subscription.
findings.fix: In the re-validation failure branch, call self._events_unsub_callback() and set it to None before clearing the identity (patch on card).

findings.title: LAN HTTP OIDC sign-in now fails on the HTTPS callback hop
findings.detail: A LAN user on http://192.168.1.20:8095 with an https callback origin passes the first is_allowed_redirect_url check, then _handle_oidc_start redirects to https://<callback>/auth/oidc/start?return_url=http://192.168.1.20... That second request is https, so the new downgrade rule returns blocked and the user gets 400 Invalid return_url. This is the http-entry flow the README documents, and it worked on cff461c5a. test_local_http_and_native_app_sign_ins_remain_supported only covers the first hop. Found by GPT Sol, confirmed in controller.py:1275-1310.
findings.fix: Only block an http return_url whose host is the request host or a configured https host, not every http target on an https request. Or validate return_url on the entry hop and carry it in the pending login instead of the query string.

findings.title: Scheme check redirect-loops behind TLS proxies without X-Forwarded-Proto
findings.detail: Still open on e296fa55b. _handle_oidc_start now defaults request_scheme to request.scheme before computing entry_url. Behind a TLS proxy that sets X-Forwarded-Host but not X-Forwarded-Proto, the request looks like http, the https entry_url origin never matches, and /auth/oidc/start redirects to itself forever.
findings.fix: When X-Forwarded-Proto is absent, use https if request.secure else the callback scheme (see suggested_fix). The genuine plain-http-on-public-host case then fails at the cookie check instead of looping. Alternative: return a 400 telling the admin to set X-Forwarded-Proto. Either way the (False, None, False) case in test_oidc_start_uses_the_browser_facing_scheme changes.

findings.title: Downgrade block misses textual IPv6 aliases and also blocks loopback
findings.detail: GPT Sol: base_url https://[fd00::1] still trusts http://[fd00:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]/ via the private-IP shortcut, since hostnames are compared as strings. Separately the new test blocks http://localhost:8765 on any https request, although RFC 8252 loopback callbacks never leave the host. No MA client uses an http loopback return_url today, so both are low impact.
findings.fix: Normalize IP literals with ipaddress before comparing, and exempt loopback targets from the downgrade rule.

findings.title: Narrowed excepts miss ValueError/TypeError from PyJWK and jwt.decode
findings.detail: A malformed JWKS key (bad RSA/EC params) or a signed token with a non-numeric nbf/iat can raise plain ValueError or TypeError inside PyJWT. The new retry loop only catches InvalidSignatureError, so these still escape as a 500 instead of a controlled sign-in failure. Needs a broken IdP. From GPT Sol on d1c3dda9b, unchanged.
findings.fix: Wrap PyJWK construction and jwt.decode and convert ValueError/TypeError to OIDCProtocolError.

findings.title: Comma-separated X-Forwarded-Proto returns 400
findings.detail: Chained proxies can send 'https, http'; the whole string fails the http/https check. Rare, and the fastmcp origin helper has the same behavior.
findings.fix: Take the first comma-separated value and strip it.

suggested_fix.description: Two parts, git apply --check clean on 6b5beb793. (1) websocket_client.py: unsubscribe the earlier event subscription when re-validation fails, so a failed re-auth on an already-subscribed socket stops receiving events. (2) controller.py: compute request_scheme after entry_url and fall back to https when request.secure, else the entry URL's scheme, so a TLS proxy without X-Forwarded-Proto doesn't loop on /auth/oidc/start.
suggested_fix.patch:
diff --git a/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/controller.py b/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/controller.py
index d7b8354..30d5ea5 100644
--- a/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/controller.py
+++ b/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/controller.py
@@ -1280,9 +1280,6 @@ class WebserverController(CoreController):
         """Bind a new OIDC sign-in to the browser and redirect to the IdP."""
         return_url = request.query.get("return_url")
         request_host = request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-Host") or request.host
-        request_scheme = request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-Proto", request.scheme).lower()
-        if request_scheme not in ("http", "https"):
-            return web.Response(status=400, text="Invalid request scheme")
         if return_url:
             valid, category = is_allowed_redirect_url(
                 return_url, request, self.base_url, self.external_url
@@ -1292,6 +1289,12 @@ class WebserverController(CoreController):
         entry_url = self.auth.get_oidc_start_url(return_url, request_host=request_host)
         if entry_url is None:
             return web.Response(status=404, text="OpenID Connect is not configured")
+        # A TLS proxy may omit X-Forwarded-Proto; redirecting on scheme alone would loop.
+        request_scheme = request.headers.get(
+            "X-Forwarded-Proto", "https" if request.secure else URL(entry_url).scheme
+        ).lower()
+        if request_scheme not in ("http", "https"):
+            return web.Response(status=400, text="Invalid request scheme")
         # Set the state cookie on the callback origin, even when opened through an alias.
         if URL(entry_url).origin() != URL(f"{request_scheme}://{request_host}").origin():
             return web.HTTPFound(entry_url)
--- a/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/websocket_client.py
+++ b/music_assistant/controllers/webserver/websocket_client.py
@@ -509,6 +509,9 @@
             user = await self.webserver.auth.authenticate_with_token(token)
             if not user:
                 self.webserver.unregister_websocket_client(self)
+                if self._events_unsub_callback:
+                    self._events_unsub_callback()
+                    self._events_unsub_callback = None
                 self._authenticated_user = None
                 self._current_token = None
                 self._token_id = None

prs.author: Simanias
prs.ci: green on 2cf720d8e
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 86a6e84fc; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: _poll_zone now drops readings when the room's zone changed during the reads, so a split no longer marks a playing room idle. _sync_groups clears the queued next item of every follower when mirroring zones, so a follower that goes solo cannot start an abandoned track. Followers could never advance anyway, so nothing needed is dropped. Ready, zero open CRITICAL/PROBLEM. Copilot has no open issues but rates it 'Needs a closer look' and asks for final human review of the zone reconciliation, so the routine left the approve to you although the rules would allow auto-approval.
prs.summary: r4337196254: after the gather, _poll_zone checks _active_zone() != zone and returns before applying transport/position. get_zone_for_room returns host.get_zones() lists, which are sorted, so list equality is stable and an unchanged zone never drops a read. A transient roomlst_to_zoneudn miss only skips one poll. The only await left after the check is _read_zone_actions in _update_zone_source. That only runs for non-MA (external) sources, where no auto-advance is armed, so there is no new stale-advance window. r4337196341: _sync_groups builds the follower set from groups[leader][1:] and calls drop_next_item(), which clears _advance_armed/_next_media and cancels the end-watch timer. Dropping cannot lose a needed item, for three reasons. First, a follower already short-circuits in poll() (synced_to) and in _watch_for_track_end (_follows_or_held clears next), so it could never have advanced. Second, a claimant passed over when owners are unresolved becomes a follower whose queue MA no longer shows. Third, the real leader is never in the follower set. An end watch in flight re-checks _follows_or_held after its await and returns. MA-initiated grouping (set_members) still relies on core stopping the child queue and on _follows_or_held, as before. Tests cover both scenarios.

prs.author: OzGav
prs.ci: green on 3ac44a43d
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 86a6e84fc; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: get_url_data now deletes the 30-day settled entry when a lookup finds the URL unknown or ambiguous. Keys match the set call and cache.get honours BYPASS_CACHE, so a refresh really re-asks and clears it. The declined CRITICAL needs three rare conditions at once, and the harm is a duplicate rather than a wrong merge. Ready. Copilot recommends approval on the head. Core touched, so it's your approve.
prs.summary: Delta 80c73af04..3ac44a43d adds an else branch in MusicBrainzAPIClient.get_url_data that calls mass.cache.delete(settled_key, provider=self.domain) whenever the lookup does not resolve to exactly one entity. The key and provider are the same as in the set call. delete() with category None matches any category, and set uses the default 0, so the entry is removed. cache.get_with_freshness returns a miss under BYPASS_CACHE for non-persistent entries, so a bypassing refresh skips the settled entry, re-queries and now drops it. That closes r4337198057. Concurrent lookups for one URL are last-writer-wins, and both writers reflect MusicBrainz at their own time, so no harmful race. A 400/401/404 response (None) also drops the settled entry, which is right for 404 and harmless otherwise because the 1-day cache re-asks. The new test drives the real set/delete sequence with BYPASS_CACHE. On the declined r4337197972: the recovered MBID is only applied at insert, after _get_library_item_by_match has run its external-id pass without it. A duplicate therefore needs a same-provider name clash, a MusicBrainz URL link, and a third library artist carrying that MBID under a name that normalises differently (localised names, P!nk/Pink). OzGav's premise that library artists carry the MusicBrainz name is not quite right: names come from the first provider. Even so the combination is rare, and the outcome (a duplicate with the same MBID, mergeable by hand) is better than the pre-PR behaviour, which merged the item into the wrong same-name artist. Decline accepted. A cheap follow-up would look up the recovered MBID before inserting.

This matches audiomuse_ai/provider.py on origin/dev line for line. The new test mocks the builder and asserts it is called with each user's id. It shows the wiring but does not exercise use_cache itself. That is acceptable because keying on positional args is the decorator's own contract, and the test mirrors the AudioMuse one.
