I grepped origin/dev for side effects. media_resolver._resolve_media_items only calls this method behind is_finite_radio, so playing or enqueuing a dynamic radio still takes the play-as-itself/dynamic-source path. managed_pool._fetch_tracks is only reached for non-dynamic sources. The controller wrapper is not an API command. The only new consumer is RadioPlaylistProvider.get_dynamic_tracks, and its callers all catch errors: radio_playlist.get_playlist_tracks catches MusicAssistantError, queue_loader autoplay suppresses or catches, music_quiz catches Exception, and smart_playlist catches MusicAssistantError. On station state: Apple's get_station_tracks is an uncached next-batch fetch, so each Endless Mix refill adds one Apple request. Pandora serves the current fragment's pending tracks and only fetches a new fragment when due. iHeart POSTs for a new batch and can raise 'out of songs', which the callers above absorb. The test replaces the old dynamic -> [] assertion (an intended behaviour change) with a dedicated case that checks availability filtering and the dynamic_tracks call. ruff and mypy are clean on the touched file, and tests/controllers/player_queues (866) plus radio_playlist pass.

prs.title: Keep a track's length after its queue moves to another player
prs.author: Simanias
prs.ci: green
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 86a6e84fc; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: Stops _cleanup_queue_audio_data (and the stale sweep) set streamdetails.buffer to None before clear(), so the writeback took the cut-off stream for a clean source and shortened the track. The PR keeps the buffer reference from the first chunk in both the single-item and the flow path. Radio and unbuffered sources fall back to the old check unchanged. Both new cases fail on dev and pass here.
prs.summary: Every release path detaches before clearing: stream_feeder _cleanup_queue_audio_data, the stale-buffer sweep, the prepare_next orphan, and get_audio_buffer's invalid-buffer reuse. AudioBuffer.clear() always sets _cancelled. The old writeback read streamdetails.buffer after the stream ended, found None, and wrote the truncated stream length as the item's duration, for example when a queue is transferred to another player. Now source_buffer is the buffer of the first chunk (a capacity reselection happens before the first yield, so that is the buffer the item really plays from), with streamdetails.buffer as fallback. Other paths: radio, realtime and unbuffered items have no buffer and behave as before. Flow mode resets source_buffer per track inside the loop. The crossfade tail accounting is unchanged. A consumer that leaves (GeneratorExit) never reaches the writeback. get_media_stream's producer-side writeback only runs when the stream finished. Players that report their own duration do not go through this code. The one theoretical change: a fully played buffer that gets cleared before the writeback runs now keeps the provider's duration instead of the measured one. That is harmless. On tests: the flow test gains a released_by_stop case, a new single-path test was added, and an existing SimpleNamespace fixture got buffer=None so the first-chunk read works; no assertion got weaker. Both new cases fail against origin/dev audio.py. Ruff and mypy are clean.

prs.title: Let the sample rates of each Raumfeld room be chosen, up to 96 kHz by default
prs.author: Simanias
prs.ci: green
prs.merge_state: merge-tree clean on origin/dev 53c876f91; review required, no auto-merge
prs.tldr: The player stops declaring 44.1-192 kHz and adds create_sample_rates_config_entry: options up to 192/24, default up to 96/24, editable per room. No room can have a stored CONF_SAMPLE_RATES, because the provider declared rates from its first commit and the core hid the entry, so everyone gets the new default. 96 kHz is strictly safer than the previous 192 kHz declaration; One S owners have to switch 176.4/192 back on. 107 raumfeld tests pass.
prs.summary: With _attr_supported_sample_rates gone, declares_supported_sample_rates is False and get_supported_sample_rates reads CONF_SAMPLE_RATES. Because the player supplies the key itself, the core's generic CONF_ENTRY_SAMPLE_RATES (default 44.1/48 at 16-bit) is filtered out, so the provider's entry and its 96/24 default are what apply. The entry is visible, advanced and requires_reload. On stored settings: SUPPORTED_SAMPLE_RATES has existed since the provider was added (fd034e289), so the sample-rate entry was never shown and nothing is stored. Every room moves to the new default, and the Raumfeld provider is not on stable. On device safety: the old code declared up to 192 kHz for every room, which the PR says drops out on 1st-gen One M, Connector and Stereo Cubes. The new 96 kHz ceiling is lower than anything shipped before. No Teufel renderer reports its rates (GetProtocolInfo lists none), so a device limited to 48 kHz cannot be ruled out from code. It would have been worse off before, and the per-room setting now lets a user lower it. The flow-mode sample-rate entry (default smart) still sits on top of these rates. Tests cover the options and default and that the player declares no rates. One existing test was refactored into a _host_room_player helper with its assertions unchanged. Ruff is clean, and merging alongside 7079 is clean.
